poc_summary: Custom driver (/poc/poc_new.c for the post-refactor 3-arg API, /poc/poc_old.c for pre_intro's 2-arg API, selected by /poc/run.sh via a grep of lib/curl_get_line.h) links directly against lib/.libs/libcurl.a and calls the internal Curl_get_line() with a FILE* created via glibc fopencookie() whose read callback always returns -1 with errno=EIO and never signals EOF — i.e. a persistent I/O read error, exactly the scenario in the bug report. A 5s alarm(2) guards against a real infinite loop so the test terminates deterministically.
explanation: root cause confirmed by source diff and by execution. post_intro's Curl_get_line() (commit 769ccb4d4261) only sets `*eof = feof(input)` after fgets() fails and keeps looping `while(1)` until `*eof` is true; with a persistent I/O error (fgets() returns NULL, ferror() true, feof() false forever) the loop never terminates - verified: the PoC hits the 5s alarm guard and prints TIMEOUT_HANG, i.e. a genuine unbounded hang (DoS), not a resource-limit artifact. pre_intro uses the older Curl_get_line(buf,input) implementation which, on fgets() returning NULL with an empty accumulated buffer, falls into the `else` branch and `break`s out of the loop immediately, returning 0 - no hang, confirming the bug is absent before the introducing commit. post_benign (the agent-composed companion fix) adds the same `if(!b && ferror(input)) return CURLE_READ_ERROR;` check as the real upstream fix (ae09e5bf0d1f) and the PoC returns promptly with RESULT=26 (CURLE_READ_ERROR), EOF=0, matching the intended fix behavior. All three revisions were built with ASan+UBSan and exercised with the identical invocation (same run.sh / same FILE* oracle); only the API shape differs across the refactor boundary, which run.sh detects generically from the header rather than from bug-dependent behavior.
